sections.heading: The three buses
points: Address: where. Its width sets how much memory can be addressed (2^n).
Data: what. Its width sets how many bits move per transfer.
Control: when and which way - read, write, clock, interrupt request.

sections.heading: Three ways to do I/O
points: Programmed (polling): the CPU asks repeatedly and wastes cycles.
Interrupt-driven: the device speaks when ready, but the CPU still moves each word.
DMA: a controller moves the whole block and interrupts once at the end.

sections.heading: What an interrupt does
points: Saves the PC and the processor status.
Jumps through the vector table to the handler, then restores and resumes.

sections.heading: Traps the quiz likes
points: Non-maskable interrupts ignore the disable flag - that is the whole point.
Interrupt-driven I/O frees the CPU from waiting, not from working.
Address bus width and data bus width answer different questions.
